items.text: There are several ways designers can minimize the likelihood of a controls accidental activation. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps the easiest way is to make sure the control is far away so that the operator is unlikely to come into accidental contact with it. <break time="0.8s" /> We could also increase the control resistance, which in turn will increase the force required for the operator to activate the control. <break time="0.8s" /> We might recess the control into the control panel or place it behind a barrier. <break time="0.8s" /> If the control is not used frequently, we can place a protective cover over it, or lock the control into position. <break time="0.8s" /> These options not only make the control harder to operate, but they create a sequence of several actions that the operator must take to activate the control. <break time="0.8s" /> If operation requires more than a single step, the operator must go through a sequence not only of actions, but also of decisions to make each action. <break time="0.8s" /> Each point in the activation process then provides an opportunity for the operator to reconsider his or her choice to activate the control.
